authority.name: City of Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety (LADBS)

codeEdition.text: Los Angeles enforces the California Building Standards Code as amended by the City, published as the Los Angeles Building, Plumbing, Electrical and Mechanical Codes inside the LA Municipal Code. LADBS told applicants that projects filed from January 1, 2023 had to meet the then-current California edition as amended by the City, and its current plumbing-code bulletins carry an effective date of January 1, 2026 and cite the Los Angeles Plumbing Code by section (for example LAPC 507.2).

permitPolicy.text: A Los Angeles property owner may take out a permit as Owner/Builder on a single-family dwelling if they show proof that they own the property and proof that they currently live at the address. LADBS also makes the owner read, initial and sign an Owner-Builder Acknowledgment and Verification of Information form before the permit is issued, and an agent can sign it only with the owner's notarized authorization.

registration.text: A contractor pulling a Los Angeles permit must produce a City of Los Angeles business tax registration certificate, or a newly paid receipt for one, on top of the state contractor's license. LADBS also asks at permit issuance for the workers' compensation certificate made out to the state license board, the contractor's license pocket ID, and notarized letters for any agent signing on the contractor's behalf.

codeItems.text: Los Angeles inspectors check water heater bracing in detail. The tank must be strapped in two places, in the upper third and the lower third, with the lower strap at least 4 inches above the control unit. Anchors must be lag screws at least 1/4 inch in diameter with at least 1-1/2 inches of thread biting into a wall stud, each with a large flat washer behind the strap. Perforated plumber's tape is not accepted on any tank over 40 gallons, and the clearance to the wall printed on the appliance nameplate is treated as critical.

Los Angeles splits water heater permits by the size of the appliance. A gas water heater is handled by the Plumbing Inspection Section only while it stays at or below 210 degrees F, 160 psi, 120 gallons and 400,000 BTU per hour. Pass any one of those and the city also requires a separate installation permit from its Pressure Vessel Section. LADBS also states that every storage heater installation needs an approved, listed, correctly sized combination temperature-and-pressure relief valve.

Los Angeles requires every newly constructed building to be an all-electric building, which the ordinance defines as having no combustion equipment for water heating among other uses. The rule is written for new construction, so it does not by itself force a gas water heater in an existing house to be swapped for an electric one, but it is the reason a new LA house will not have a gas heater to replace.

Los Angeles prices a thermal expansion tank, an earthquake gas shutoff valve and a pressure regulating valve as separate permit items on its plumbing schedule, so each one added alongside a water heater is written onto the permit and inspected rather than treated as part of the heater.

water-heater-replacement.requirement: Los Angeles requires a plumbing permit to install or replace a gas water heater, and LADBS issues it as an express permit with no plan check; the inspector looks at the two seismic straps, the relief valve and anything added with the heater.
water-heater-replacement.fee: Water heater and vent or heat exchanger $28.00; Thermal Expansion Tank $15.00; minimum $90 if applying for 2 or more items, minimum $55 for one item costing less than $55; permit issuing fee $23.00 if the sub-total is over $90; plus 3% D.S.C.S. and 6% System's Surcharge, $1.00 minimum each

garbage-disposal-replacement.requirement: Replacing a garbage disposal in Los Angeles needs a plumbing permit, which LADBS treats as an express permit for replacing a plumbing fixture, and the city charges less for a swap than for a brand-new fixture.
garbage-disposal-replacement.fee: Garbage Disposal, replace or remove existing $10.00; Garbage Disposal, new $23.00; minimum $55 if applying for one item costing less than $55; plus 3% D.S.C.S. and 6% System's Surcharge, $1.00 minimum each

plumber-service-call.requirement: Los Angeles charges a plumbing permit per item of work, and a small repair still runs into the city's minimum permit charge; a failed inspection that brings the inspector back out is billed as an extra trip.
plumber-service-call.fee: Replace or remove existing fixtures $10.00 each; Waste & Vent Alter/Repair $10.00; Sewer Alter/Repair/Cap $24.00; Extra Trip $90.00; Miscellaneous Permit $90.00; minimum $90 if applying for 2 or more items, minimum $55 for one item costing less than $55

electrician-service-call.requirement: Los Angeles charges an electrical permit by the circuit or by the count of devices, so even a small job lands on the city's minimum permit charge, and LADBS bills an extra trip when the inspector has to return.
electrician-service-call.fee: General use 120V branch circuits, 1-10 circuits $17.00 each; Receptacle, light, switch or telephone units, 1-5 units $18.00 total, 6-10 units $22.00 total; Extra Trip $90.00 each; Miscellaneous Permit $90.00; minimum $90 if applying for 2 or more items, minimum $55 for one item costing less than $55; permit issuing fee $23.00 if the sub-total is over $90

smoke-detector-replacement.requirement: Los Angeles treats smoke detectors in a house, duplex or apartment unit as electrical work needing a permit, and LADBS lists it as an express permit so no plan check is involved.
smoke-detector-replacement.fee: SFD and Apartment Smoke Detectors, 1 residential unit $15.00; each additional residential unit in a multi-dwelling occupancy $12.00; minimum $55 if applying for one item costing less than $55
